title: Reservation token and micro-defrag cue for hotpage stability
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Paged KV workloads for streaming generation suffer from short-lived thrash where hot pages are repeatedly evicted and reallocated during bursty sequences (continuous-batching path). This PR introduces a lightweight 'reservation token' that callers in the continuous-batching fast-path can attach to pages they consider hot, plus a compact 'micro-defrag' cue in page metadata to avoid large reallocation passes. Together these reduce eviction churn, stabilize kernel hot-set locality, and give the scheduler a low-cost signal to prefer reserved pages for low-latency kernels.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a reservation token API: allocator.reserve(token_id, page_id) and release semantics with optional time-decay when callers fail to release (configurable). Reservations are cheap (atomic tag on page metadata) and do not change ownership semantics.
- Adds a 2-bit micro-defrag cue per page (NONE | SOFT | STRONG) that lets the background defragmenter prioritize ranges without triggering full-copy compaction for short-lived fragmentation. The cue is set by the allocator on short evict+realloc cycles.
- Scheduler hint plumbing: the kernel scheduler reads reservation bits to bias placement and kernel selection for low-p99 paths (e.g., single-token streaming kernels). This is a soft preference and falls back when capacity is constrained.
- Continuous-batching integration: the fast-path attaches temporary reservation tokens for prefixes that are likely to be re-opened (chat threads, repeated completion tokens). This prevents immediate eviction during back-to-back small requests.
- Telemetry and feature flags: new metrics page_reserved_count, reservation_evictions, microdefrag_hits, microdefrag_promoted. Feature-gated behind runtime.kv.reservations=true with staged rollout.

Performance impact (internal bench):
- Chat-sim workload (N=1000 concurrent short-streams): +9% throughput, -12% p99 token latency, -24% KV evictions vs baseline.
- Long-sequence steady-state: negligible overhead (±1% throughput).
- Memory churn on synthetic churn test: 30% fewer full-defrag runs across a 30-minute run.

Compatibility and safety:
- Backwards-compatible: reservation bits are optional; older nodes ignore them. The allocator tolerates missing token support by treating reservations as no-ops.
- Safety: reservation lifetime is bounded (configurable TTL) to avoid permanent leaks; the release path is idempotent and uses epoch counters to avoid ABA on quick reuses.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for reserve/release, TTL expiry, and race scenarios added in tests/kv_reservation_unittest.rs.
- Integration benchmarks added under perf/bench/chat_sim.py with harness toggles.
- Stress job that runs continuous-batching generator for 4 hours in CI-infra (runs as perf job in our infra).

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag (off by default).
2) Canary on dedicated pool with synthetic workload.
3) Enable telemetry for 48h, verify reservation_evictions drop and no increases in out-of-memory events.
4) Gradual ramp to hosted fleet across regions.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests

Related/References: ENG-1721 (hotset stability), PERF-438 (kv eviction metric), design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/board/ENG-1721/reservations-design (internal), prior allocator work (see linked PRs for block allocator reuse).

review_comments: Gavin Morris (2026-02-20): Nice approach. Two asks: make the reservation TTL configurable per-node and add a metric for reservations that outlive their expected TTL. Also please ensure the reserve path is lock-free for the hot path.

Aisha Patel (2026-02-20): Addressed both. TTL is exposed via runtime.kv.reservation_ttl_seconds and a new metric reservation_ttl_expiry_count is emitted. Reserve uses an atomic tag update with a tiny CAS loop (see paged_allocator.rs).
Lena Zhou (2026-02-22): There was a race in the release path during stress tests where a page was reserved, released and re-reserved rapidly. Could we use an epoch counter to avoid ABA?
Aisha Patel (2026-02-23): Implemented epoch counter on page metadata and added unit test that reproduces the race.
Marcus Rivera (2026-02-26): CI flaky: perf job hit a transient network failure on the 4h stress run. Rerunning now.
CI Bot (2026-02-27): perf job rerun passed. All checks green.
Marcus Rivera (2026-02-28): LGTM after the epoch counter fix and docs update. Approving.
release_notes: Introduce KV reservation tokens and micro-defrag cue to reduce eviction churn for continuous-batching workloads. Feature-gated; metrics added for observability. Expected improvements for chat-style short-stream workloads.
